exposure: obstetric history (number of children, first delivery method)
outcome: preference for mode of delivery (normal delivery vs. Cesarean Section)
cohort: 400 pregnant women referred to a hospital in Tehran, Iran in 2016.
finding: Pregnant women's preference for delivery mode was significantly correlated with their views towards normal delivery, occupation, education level, number of children, first delivery method, and participation in childbirth education classes.
mod_finding: Women with lower scores (negative views towards normal delivery) preferred Cesarean Section, while employed, university-educated women with a history of normal delivery and participation in childbirth education classes showed a greater tendency towards normal delivery.
